contexts: day surgery unit, about 6,000 adult procedures a year
four-factor risk score and one to three agents
paper drug section of the anaesthetic record
60 hours of fellow time for record reading
reading: Prophylaxis sits between the risk score and two opposite harms: under-prophylaxis leading to rescue treatment (c2) and over-prophylaxis leading to sedation and delayed discharge (c4). Adherence is likely to be partial (c1). The recovery log defines cases reliably enough (c3), while the paper drug record limits how many patients can be examined, which favours sampling cases and controls. Longer operations, opioids and sicker patients push toward both more prophylaxis and more nausea, which is the main confounding path.
